He declared for the [[2013 NBA Draft]] after completing his junior season for the [[2012–13 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2012–13 team]]. He is the son of [[National Basketball Association]] [[NBA All-Star Game|All-Star]] [[Tim Hardaway]]. As a [[high school basketball]] player, he was a three-time All-City performer for [[Miami Palmetto High School]]. As a freshman during the [[2010–11 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]], earned four [[Big Ten Conference]] Freshman of the Week awards, including three in the final four weeks during which he averaged over 20 [[point (basketball)|points]] a game to help the [[2010–11 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2010–11 team]] to climb up to fourth in the [[2010–11 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season]] standings. He was an honorable mention All-Big Ten selection and a unanimous Big Ten All-Freshman team selection following the season. He established the Michigan freshman record for single-season three point shots made. He was a 2011 [[Collegeinsider.com]] Freshmen All-America selection and participated as a member of Team USA in the [[2011 FIBA Under-19 World Championship]]. As a sophomore for the [[2011–12 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|2011–12 team]], he earned the [[2011–12 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2011–12 All-Big Ten]] 3rd team recognition. He earned [[2012–13 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season|2012–13 All-Big Ten]] (1st team: coaches and 2nd team: media) recognition. ==High School== Hardaway, who is the son of Yolanda and NBA All-Star [[Tim Hardaway]], spent his freshman year at [[Palmer Trinity School]] before transferring to [[Miami Palmetto High School]].{{cite web|url=http://www.annarbor.com/sports/um-basketball/while-creating-his-own-game-michigan-freshman-guard-tim-hardaway-jr-has-shades-of-his-father/|title=Michigan freshman guard Tim Hardaway Jr. has shades of his father's game|accessdate=2011-02-28|date=2010-08-22|work=[[AnnArbor.com]]|author=Rothstein, Michael}} As a freshman, he played [[high school football]] for a year before focusing on basketball.{{cite web|url=http://www.michigandaily.com/sports/shadow-name-how-tim-hardaway-jr-has-formed-his-basketball-identity?page=0,4|title=The Shadow of a Name: How Tim Hardaway Jr. has formed his basketball identity|accessdate=2012-01-28|date=2011-10-30|work=[[Michigan Daily]]|author=Estes, Ben}} As he focused on basketball, he had a tumultuous relationship with his father, who acted like a second coach, and was overlooked by most [[college basketball]] programs. Michigan was the first school to contact him, communicating by mail during his sophomore year. During his junior year, Michigan [[head coach]] [[John Beilein]] invited him on an unofficial visit to watch [[2008–09 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|Michigan]] play #4 [[2008–09 Duke Blue Devils men's basketball team|Duke]] on December 6 to see unranked Michigan pull an upset. The 81–73 victory was an important win for the program.{{vcite web|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=283410130|title=Sims scores career-high 28 as Michigan limits Duke's outside effectiveness|accessdate=December 06, 2008|date=December 06, 2008|publisher=ESPN Internet Ventures|work=[[ESPN.com]]}} In the summer before his senior season, he attended Beilein’s Elite Camp in [[Ann Arbor, Michigan]], receiving an offer that he accepted. At the time, Hardaway was unranked in the [[Rivals.com]] Top-150 and his only other offers were from [[Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball|Minnesota]] and [[Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball|Kansas State]]. He was a first team All-City selection in 2009 and 2010 after being a third team selection in 2008. During his 2009–10 senior season, he averaged 31.7 points, 7.3 [[rebound (basketball)|rebounds]] and 4.0 [[assist (basketball)|assists]].{{cite web|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/hardawayjr_tim00.html|title=10 Tim Hardaway Jr.|accessdate=2011-02-27|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]}} In the Florida state championships against [[Pine Crest School]], he posted 42 points against [[Brandon Knight (basketball)|Brandon Knight]] who had 36. [[ESPN]] rated him as the 93rd best player and 28th best shooting guard in the class of 2010.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/recruiting/player/_/id/66934|title=Tim Hardaway, Jr.|accessdate=2011-02-27|publisher=[[ESPN]]}} [[Scout.com]] rated him as the 36th best shooting guard in his class.{{cite web|url=http://michigan.scout.com/a.z?s=162&p=8&c=1&nid=3798656|title=Tim Hardaway|accessdate=2011-02-27|publisher=[[Scout.com]]}} He was not top-ranked by [[Rivals.com]].{{cite web|url=http://rivals.yahoo.com/basketballrecruiting/basketball/recruiting/player-Tim-Hardaway-70973;_ylt=AlwlcN3T.ka5q1OnnBO4Ut7SO5B4|title=Time Hardaway|accessdate=2011-02-27|publisher=[[Rivals.com]]}} Hardaway has played summer [[Amateur Athletic Union]] (AAU) basketball for both the South Florida Heat and Chicago's Mac Irvin Fire, where he teamed with {{convert|7|ft|m|2|adj=on}} [[Meyers Leonard]] and [[McDonald's All-American]] [[Jereme Richmond]].{{cite web|url=http://blogs.suntimes.com/hoopsreport/2013/04/fire_wins_meanstreets_and_wolv.html|title=Mac Irvin Fire wins, Meanstreets and Wolves impress|accessdate=2013-04-12|date=2013-04-10|work=[[Chicago Sun-Times]]|author=Henricksen, Joe}} {{College Athlete Recruit Start|40=no|collapse=no|year=2010}} {{College Athlete Recruit Entry | recruit = Tim Hardaway, Jr. | position = [[Shooting Guard|SG]] | hometown = Miami, Florida | highschool = [[Palmer Trinity School|Palmer]] (Freshman), (FL)

Michigan 66 (1-0, 1-0 home)|accessdate=2011-02-28|date=2010-11-13|publisher=[[ESPN]]}} he was soon in a shooting slump that saw him shoot 4 for 30 on his [[field goal (basketball)|field goals]] in late November games against [[2010–11 Syracuse Orange men's basketball team|Syracuse]] and {{cbb link|2010|sex=men|team=UTEP Miners|school=University of Texas at El Paso|title=UTEP}}.{{cite web|url=http://www.annarbor.com/sports/um-basketball/michigan-forward-tim-hardaway-jr-breaks-out-of-his-funk-and-jordan-morgans-foul-trouble/|title=Michigan forward Tim Hardaway Jr. breaks out of his funk and Jordan Morgan's foul trouble|accessdate=2011-02-28|date=2010-12-01|work=[[AnnArbor.com]]|author=Rothstein, Michael}} These games marked the beginning of a slump during which he went 13 consecutive games without achieving a 50% [[field goal percentage]] and 19 games without exceeding that number.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/mens-college-basketball/player/gamelog/_/id/51270/year/2011/tim-hardaway-jr|title=Tim Hardaway Jr. Game-by-Game Stats (2010-11)|accessdate=2011-11-26|publisher=[[ESPN]]}} [[File:20101223 Tim Hardaway, Jr..jpg|thumb|left|Hardaway shooting a [[free throw]] (12-23-2010)]] Hardaway earned four Big Ten Freshman of the week awards. On December 27, the [[Big Ten Conference]] named Hardaway co-freshman of the week along with [[Jared Sullinger]].{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/122710aac.html|title=Michigan and Ohio State Claim Weekly Conference Honors: Michigan and Ohio State earn conference recognition|accessdate=2010-12-28|date=2010-12-27|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]}} On December 23, 2010, against {{cbb link|2010|sex=men|team=Bryant Bulldogs|school=Bryant University|title=Bryant University}}, [[2010–11 Michigan Wolverines men's basketball team|the team]] tied its December 13, 2008 single-game school record of 16 [[three point field goal]]s made,{{cite web|url=http://www.mgoblue.com/auto_pdf/p_hotos/s_chools/mich/sports/m-baskbl/auto_pdf/bkm-all-time-records|title=All-Time Records|accessdate=2011-01-16|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]|work=MGoBlue.com|page=6}} and Hardaway was one of three Wolverines to make 4 three point shots.{{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/boxscore?gameId=303570130|title=Bryant U 71 (1-10, 0-1 NEC): Michigan 87 (10-2, 9-0 home)|accessdate=2011-02-03|date=2010-12-23|publisher=[[ESPN]]}} It was Hardaway's first 20-point game. On February 14, Hardaway earned his second Big Ten Conference Freshman of the week recognition for his first career [[Double (basketball)#Double-double|double-double]] on February 9 against [[2010-11 Northwestern Wildcats men's basketball team|Northwestern]] (17 points and career-high 10 rebounds){{cite web|url=http://espn.go.com/ncb/boxscore?gameId=310400130|title=Northwestern 66 (14-9, 4-8 Big Ten); Michigan 73 (16-10, 6-7 Big Ten)|accessdate=2011-02-15|date=2011-02-12|publisher=[[ESPN]]}}{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/021411aab.html|title=Wisconsin and Michigan Receive Men's Basketball Weekly Honors: Wisconsin's Jordan Taylor earns Player of the Week; Illinois 54 (17-9, 7-6 Big Ten)|accessdate=2011-02-22|date=2011-02-16|publisher=[[ESPN]]}} On February 28, Hardaway earned his third consecutive and fourth overall Big Ten Conference Freshman of the week recognition.{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/022811aaa.html|title=Purdue and Michigan Garner Conference Recognition: Purdue's JaJuan Johnson earns Player of the Week while Michigan's Tim Hardaway Jr. was tabbed Freshman of the Week.|accessdate=2011-02-28|date=2011-02-28|publisher=[[Big Ten Conference]]}} During the week, Hardaway extended his double-digit scoring streak to eleven by posting 22 points against [[2010-11 Minnesota Golden Gophers men's basketball team|Minnesota]] on February 26 after scoring 16 against #12 [[2010-11 Wisconsin Badgers men's basketball team|Wisconsin]] on February 23.{{cite web|url=http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/boxscore?gameId=310540130|title=(12) Wisconsin 53 (21-6, 11-4 Big Ten); As a result of the three consecutive freshman of the week performances and a final week in which he scored 20 in the team's only game, he averaged 20.1 points during the final 7 games of the regular season while the team won six of its final eight, which enabled it to finish tied for fourth for the conference standings and earn the fourth seed in the [[2011 Big Ten Conference Men's Basketball Tournament]].{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/spec-rel/030611aac.html|title=Big Ten Announces Bracket For 2011 Men's Basketball Tournament: Ohio State earns No. 1 seed for fifth time in tournament history|accessdate=2011-03-07|date=2011-03-06|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]}} He led the team in scoring during the 18-game conference schedule of the [[2010–11 Big Ten Conference men's basketball season]], edging out teammate [[Darius Morris]] by a 268–263 (14.9–14.6 points per game) margin. He also led the team in [[steal (basketball)|steals]] (1.17/game), [[free throw percentage]] (71.2%, min 2.0 made/game), three point shooting percentage (44.2%, min 1.0 made/game), and three point shots made per game (2.56) over the course of the conference schedule.{{cite web|url=http://www.bigten.org/sports/m-baskbl/stats/2010-2011/confonly.html|title=2010-11 Big Ten Conference: CONFERENCE BASKETBALL STATISTICS|accessdate=2011-03-05|date=2011-03-07|publisher=[[CBS Interactive]]}} Following the Big Ten Conference season, Hardaway was an honorable mention All-Big Ten selection by both the coaches and the media.
